claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

First, could you please tell me how many children you're looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! Yes, I'd like to check if I can claim Child Benefit. I have one child - Alex, who's 8 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! Let me ask a few more questions to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Do you currently live in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. Now, regarding Alex:

Are you responsible for Alex? This would usually mean either:
- Alex lives with you, or
- You're paying at least the same amount as Child Benefit (or the equivalent in kind) towards looking after them, for example on food, clothes or pocket money

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives with me at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Lovely, thank you. Just a couple more questions to make sure we cover everything:

Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. And one final question:

Is Alex currently in any of the following situations?
- In hospital for more than 12 weeks
- In care (looked after by a local council) for more than 8 weeks
- In residential accommodation paid for by the local council

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, actually Alex has been in hospital for a while now - it's been about 3 or 4 months.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know. Since Alex has been in hospital for more than 12 weeks, your Child Benefit eligibility may be affected. However, there can be exceptions to this rule.

Could you tell me whether you regularly spend money on Alex while they are in hospital? This could include things like bringing them food, clothes, toys, or other items.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do. I still buy things for Alex - clothes, magazines, and their favorite snacks and treats when I visit.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. That's helpful to know.

Just to confirm one more thing: Is Alex in a hospital in the UK, or is Alex in a hospital abroad?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex is in a hospital here in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for confirming that. Based on all the information you've provided, I now have enough details to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, **you should be eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's a summary of your situation:

**For Alex (age 8):** ✅ Eligible

Although Alex has been in hospital for more than 12 weeks, which would normally affect your entitlement, there is an exception that applies in your case. Since:
- Alex is in a UK hospital, and
- You regularly spend money on Alex (buying clothes, magazines, snacks and treats)

...you meet the exception criteria that allows Child Benefit to continue.

**Important:** You should inform HM Revenue and Customs (HMRC) about Alex's hospital stay if you haven't already. You can do this by filling in an online form or contacting HMRC by phone or post. This ensures your claim remains valid and they're aware of your circumstances.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?
